dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin.
Hi Kevin! Great, thanks for picking up. This is Ricardo Herrera. I'm on speaker, I've got my hands full, so tell me if I'm hard to hear.
No, you're coming through fine. What can I do for you, Ricardo?

Okay, so, wonderful, here's the deal. We got just a dusting overnight, right? Barely anything. But it's freezing out there, this cold snap, and the plow came through this morning and left a berm across the end of our shared driveway. A wall of packed, icy stuff. Two cars can't get out.
Ah, yeah. The plow pushes it right across the mouth of the driveway. That's a common complaint. Is this a driveway you share with a neighbor?

Yes! Shared with the house next door. We both come out onto the same strip, so the berm blocks both of us. And I'm sorry, but it's a dusting! Why is there a wall of ice for a dusting? It's frozen solid, I can't even break it with the shovel.

Right, okay. So that's probably leftover from the last storm, refrozen, and the plow scraped it up and pushed it over. I'm writing this down. Berm across shared driveway, ice, not much new snow. Do you have the street name?
Oh, great question. Um, I'd rather not give the address on this call, honestly. Is that okay? I just want to report it and ask for sand.
Hm. Well, I can log it as a general complaint, but a crew can't really go fix something without knowing where it is. The street at least, or a cross street?
Yeah, no, I get that. Let me think. Can you just note it and I'll call back with the street? I've got to figure out something first.
Sure, I'll note it as is. Just so you know, without a location it won't go to a crew. Whenever you call back, give the street and we'll get it moving.
Wonderful. Great. Okay. And the sand, can somebody bring sand? Because even if I chip out the berm, the whole driveway is a sheet of ice. My neighbor already slipped once.

Sand, yeah. We don't usually deliver to driveways. The plow trucks sand the roads. But residents can usually pick up a bucket or so of sand from a public works pile. Let me double check that, hold on one second.
Sure, sure, take your time!

Okay, I'm back. Yes, there's a sand pile for residents. You bring your own bucket or bags and a shovel, and it's for your own use. It's at the public works yard. I can give you the directions on that.
Great! Oh, that's wonderful. Hang on, let me grab a pen. Okay, go ahead.
So the yard is off the main road out toward the north end, you'll see the signs for the Public Works entrance. Do you know where the city garage is?
I think so. Yeah. Is that near the, um, the big lot by the transfer area?
Close enough, yeah. The pile is toward the front. If you get lost, call and we'll talk you in. They're open weekdays during regular hours, so you could go this afternoon.

Perfect. This afternoon works. Okay, and one more thing, a little embarrassing. If somebody does come out to look at the berm, there's a webcam on the garage that points at the driveway, and I forgot to cover it. I mean, it's fine, it's just my camera, but I didn't want a crew thinking I'm spying. Not that I'd mind.
No, that's fine. Nobody's going to worry about a camera on a garage. Honestly the guys are mostly just trying to get through their route.

Right, right. But I'm just saying, it caught the whole thing this morning. The plow comes by, pushes this huge pile, and just keeps going. Didn't even slow down! Great footage of my frustration. I was standing there with a coffee.

Yeah. A lot of times the driver can't see the driveway until they've already pushed. It's not great. Hold on, let me read back what I've got. Berm across shared driveway after the plow, icy, cold snap, dusting of snow, caller wants sand and will give the street later. Did I miss anything?
No, that's it! That's perfect. Oh, and my number, in case somebody needs to call me. It's 401-555-0183.
Got it, 401-555-0183. Under Herrera?
Yes, Herrera, H-E-R-R-E-R-A. Ricardo.

Great. So, Ricardo, a little tip. If the berm is mostly refrozen plowed snow, and you can chip at it from the top, a flat shovel or a pick sometimes works better than a regular snow shovel. Salt first, if you have it, then sand over after.
Okay, I've got a bag of ice melt in the garage. That's actually a good idea. I'll hit it with that and then go get the sand. Wonderful.
There you go. And call back with the street, and I'll make sure it's put in for the crew to look at.
Will do. Thanks, Kevin. Really, great help. Have a good one!
You too, Ricardo. Stay warm out there.
